times.label: Before the story
The disappearance of Silver Blaze and the murder of John Straker
times.quote: he had been there at the time of the struggle
times.note: Holmes (¶226): frightened at the glare, the horse lashed out and its steel shoe struck Straker on the forehead; as he fell, his knife gashed his thigh. Then the horse bolted (¶231).

times.label: Tuesday evening: telegrams from Ross and Gregory
times.quote: On Tuesday evening I received telegrams

times.label: Wednesday: Holmes broods and waits for news
times.quote: From hour to hour yesterday I expected to hear that he had been found
times.note: Also the 'whole day' of ¶4, when Holmes paces the room and the papers are sent up; and the day Holmes sends his special wire to Dartmoor (¶31).

times.label: The arrest of Fitzroy Simpson
times.quote: promptly found and arrested the man upon whom suspicion naturally rested
times.note: The day after the stranger's visit ('the evening before', ¶40), so Tuesday; Simpson's statement is made then.

times.label: Watson reads the Telegraph and the Chronicle on the case
times.quote: I have seen what the _Telegraph_ and the _Chronicle_ have to say
times.note: Some time before the train journey; not otherwise dated.

times.label: Thursday morning, at breakfast in Baker Street
times.quote: as we sat down together to our breakfast one morning
times.note: The day is given in ¶13: 'this is Thursday morning'.

times.label: Thursday, leaving Paddington by train
times.quote: the bundle of fresh papers which he had procured at Paddington

times.label: Thursday, on the train, Reading far behind
times.quote: We had left Reading far behind us

times.label: Thursday, on the train beyond Reading: Holmes times the train and states the case
times.quote: Our rate at present is fifty-three and a half miles an hour

times.label: Straker begins riding as Colonel Ross's jockey (about twelve years before)
times.quote: He has served the Colonel for five years as jockey and for seven as trainer
times.note: Five years as jockey, then seven as trainer, up to the present.

times.label: Straker becomes the Colonel's trainer (about seven years before)
times.quote: for seven as trainer

times.label: Silver Blaze is foaled (some four years before)
times.quote: He is now in his fifth year

times.label: The villas to the north are built by a Tavistock contractor
times.quote: which have been built by a Tavistock contractor

times.label: Fitzroy Simpson squanders his fortune on the turf
times.quote: who had squandered a fortune upon the turf

times.label: Simpson registers bets against the favourite
times.quote: bets to the amount of five thousand pounds had been registered by him against the favourite

times.label: Simpson comes down to Dartmoor for information
times.quote: he had come down to Dartmoor in the hope of getting some information

times.label: Monday, nine o'clock: the stables are locked up
times.quote: the stables were locked up at nine o'clock
times.note: After the horses were exercised and watered that evening.

times.label: Monday evening: two lads at supper in Straker's kitchen
times.quote: Two of the lads walked up to the trainer's house, where they had supper in the kitchen
times.note: The people at the house eat the same dish as Hunter (¶37).

times.label: Monday, a few minutes after nine: Edith Baxter carries the supper down
times.quote: At a few minutes after nine the maid, Edith Baxter, carried down to the stables his supper

times.label: Monday night: the stranger stops the maid thirty yards from the stables
times.quote: Edith Baxter was within thirty yards of the stables, when a man appeared out of the darkness

times.label: Monday night: the maid reaches the stable window
times.quote: ran past him to the window through which she was accustomed to hand the meals

times.label: Monday night: the stranger comes up to the window and speaks to Hunter
times.quote: She had begun to tell him of what had happened, when the stranger came up again

times.label: Monday night: Hunter runs for the dog; the maid flees, the stranger leans through the window
times.quote: He sprang up and rushed across the stable to unloose the dog

times.label: Monday night, a minute later: Hunter locks the door and runs out with the dog; the stranger is gone
times.quote: A minute later, however, when Hunter rushed out with the hound he was gone

times.label: Monday night: the maid back at the house
times.quote: The girl fled away to the house

times.label: Monday night: Hunter eats his curried mutton
times.quote: the remains of his supper left by the stable-lad
times.note: Not ordered against the stranger's visit or Hunter's message.

times.label: Monday night: the other lads return; Hunter sends a message to Straker
times.quote: Hunter waited until his fellow-grooms had returned, when he sent a message to the trainer

times.label: Monday night: the storm
times.quote: he had been out in the storm of the night before
times.note: Rain heard at one in the morning (¶32); not otherwise bounded.

times.label: Tuesday, one in the morning: Mrs. Straker finds her husband dressing
times.quote: Mrs. Straker, waking at one in the morning, found that he was dressing

times.label: Tuesday, after one: Straker leaves the house in his mackintosh
times.quote: he pulled on his large mackintosh and left the house

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: Silver Blaze is taken from his stall
times.quote: the favourite's stall was empty
times.note: Holmes (¶219–220): Straker went down in the dead of the night and took out Silver Blaze; the dog, knowing him, did not bark enough to wake the lads. Hunter locked the door when he ran out (¶31); the door was found open at seven.

times.label: Tuesday, seven in the morning: Mrs. Straker wakes; her husband is not back
times.quote: Mrs. Straker awoke at seven in the morning

times.label: Tuesday morning: Mrs. Straker and the maid at the stables; door open, Hunter drugged, stall empty
times.quote: set off for the stables. The door was open

times.label: Tuesday morning: the search party on the knoll
times.quote: on ascending the knoll near the house

times.label: Tuesday morning: the overcoat on the furze-bush and Straker's body in the hollow
times.quote: at the bottom of this was found the dead body of the unfortunate trainer

times.label: Hunter recovers from his stupor
times.quote: Hunter, on recovering from his stupor

times.label: The analysis of Hunter's supper
times.quote: an analysis has shown

times.label: A large reward is offered for the horse
times.quote: although a large reward has been offered

times.label: Inspector Gregory arrives on the case
times.quote: On his arrival he promptly found and arrested the man

times.label: Next Tuesday: the Wessex Cup is run
times.quote: at the fall of the flag next Tuesday
times.note: The start of the Wessex Cup, seen through Watson's field-glass: 'An excellent start!' (¶199).

times.label: Thursday evening: arrival at Tavistock station, met by Colonel Ross and Inspector Gregory
times.quote: It was evening before we reached the little town of Tavistock

times.label: Thursday evening, a minute later: the drive in the landau through Tavistock and out towards King's Pyland
times.quote: A minute later we were all seated in a comfortable landau
times.note: The talk of ¶51–68 happens during this drive, before the light fails.

times.label: Simpson twice lodges at Tavistock in the summer
times.quote: He has twice lodged at Tavistock in the summer
times.note: Earlier summers; not ordered against his coming down this time.

times.label: The powdered opium is obtained (Gregory guesses in London)
times.quote: The opium was probably brought from London
times.note: Gregory's guess; it would come before the opium reached Hunter's supper, but the story does not fix when or by whom.

times.label: The duplicate key is thrown away (Gregory's guess)
times.quote: The key, having served its purpose, would be hurled away
times.note: Part of the police theory; the story has not shown that any such key exists.

times.label: Simpson loses his cravat (his own claim)
times.quote: declares that he had lost it
times.note: Simpson's claim. The maid saw the stranger wearing it on Monday evening (¶35), but the story does not say when he says he lost it.

times.label: Monday night: a party of gypsies camped within a mile of the spot of the murder
times.quote: a party of gypsies encamped on Monday night within a mile of the spot

times.label: Tuesday: the gypsies are gone
times.quote: On Tuesday they were gone

times.label: Gregory examines every stable and out-house in and around Tavistock
times.quote: I have also examined every stable and out-house in Tavistock

times.label: The police examine the Mapleton stables
times.quote: We have, however, examined the stables

times.label: Silas Brown places large bets on the Wessex Cup
times.quote: is known to have had large bets upon the event

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: Straker picks up the knife from the dressing-table as he leaves the room (his wife's account)
times.quote: he had picked it up as he left the room
times.note: Just before he leaves the house (t.straker_leaves); the text does not order it more finely.

times.label: Straker's body is brought back to his villa
times.quote: Straker was brought back here, I presume?

times.label: The Inspector takes the things in Straker's pockets and puts them in a tin box
times.quote: I have the things themselves in the sitting-room

times.label: Mrs. Straker tells the police about the knife and about Derbyshire
times.quote: His wife tells us that the knife had lain upon the dressing-table

times.label: Letters for William Derbyshire are now and then addressed to Straker's house (Mrs. Straker's account)
times.quote: occasionally his letters were addressed here

times.label: Madame Lesurier makes out the milliner's account to William Derbyshire
times.quote: made out by Madame Lesurier, of Bond Street, to William Derbyshire
times.note: Before Straker's death, since the account was in his pockets; the story gives no closer date.

times.label: A garden-party at Plymouth "some little time ago" (Holmes's claim; Mrs. Straker denies it)
times.quote: Surely I met you in Plymouth at a garden-party some little time ago
times.note: Holmes's claim; Mrs. Straker says he is mistaken.

times.label: Thursday evening, a few minutes later: the landau pulls up at Straker's villa
times.quote: A few minutes later our driver pulled up at a neat little red-brick villa

times.label: Thursday evening: in the sitting-room, the Inspector lays out Straker's things
times.quote: We all filed into the front room and sat round the central table

times.label: Thursday evening: Mrs. Straker meets them in the passage as they leave the sitting-room
times.quote: As we emerged from the sitting-room a woman, who had been waiting in the passage

times.label: Friday: the inquest on Straker
times.quote: The inquest is to-morrow.

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: the overcoat is laid across the furze-bush
times.quote: it was laid across the bush
times.note: Holmes (¶226): Straker had already, in spite of the rain, taken off his overcoat to do his delicate task. No wind that night (¶96).

times.label: A wax vesta, half burned, comes to lie in the mud of the hollow
times.quote: It was a wax vesta half burned
times.note: The story does not say when or by whom. Holmes expected to find it. It lay buried in the mud before Thursday's search.

times.label: Silver Blaze casts the horseshoe the Inspector now holds
times.quote: a cast horseshoe of Silver Blaze
times.note: Not dated.

times.label: Silver Blaze is entered for the Wessex Cup
times.quote: remove our horse's name from the entries for the Cup
times.note: Not dated; before the race.

times.label: Many feet trample the hollow since Monday night; the matting is laid at the side
times.quote: many feet have been here since Monday night
times.note: The matting (¶99) is laid at some time after the body was found and before Thursday.

times.label: The Inspector bags Straker's boot, Simpson's shoe and the cast horseshoe
times.quote: In this bag I have one of the boots which Straker wore
times.note: Not dated more finely.

times.label: Gregory examines the ground for a hundred yards in each direction
times.quote: I have examined the ground very carefully for a hundred yards in each direction

times.label: Thursday evening: after a short walk across the moor, the party at the brink of the hollow by the furze-bush
times.quote: A short walk across the moor took us to the hollow in which the body had been found

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes descends into the hollow, studies the mud and finds the vesta
times.quote: descending into the hollow, he pushed the matting into a more central position

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes compares the boots with the marks, then climbs to the rim and searches the ferns
times.quote: Then he clambered up to the rim of the hollow

times.label: Thursday evening, at sunset: Holmes and Watson walk slowly across the moor from the hollow
times.quote: Holmes and I walked slowly across the moor
times.note: The walk planned in ¶109, now told. The sun is beginning to sink behind the Mapleton stables.

times.label: Thursday evening: Colonel Ross and the Inspector turn back towards Straker's house
times.quote: He turned back with the Inspector

times.label: Thursday evening: the drive together into Tavistock; Holmes speaks of the sheep and of the dog in the night-time
times.quote: Drive on, coachman!

times.label: Friday: Holmes's work on the ground (planned)
times.quote: that I may know my ground to-morrow

times.label: Thursday evening, a few minutes later: at the long hollow towards Mapleton, Holmes finds the horse's track
times.quote: a few more minutes brought us to the hollow in question

times.label: Thursday evening: across dry turf, the tracks are picked up again close to Mapleton, with a man's track beside the horse's
times.quote: only to pick them up once more quite close to Mapleton

times.label: Thursday evening: they follow the double track towards King's Pyland; Watson sees the tracks coming back
times.quote: we both followed along after it

times.label: Thursday evening: they follow the return track to the asphalt paving before the Mapleton gates
times.quote: It ended at the paving of asphalt which led up to the gates of the Mapleton stables

times.label: Thursday evening: at the Mapleton gates, the groom Dawson runs out, then Silas Brown strides out
times.quote: As we approached, a groom ran out from them

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes goes in with Silas Brown to his parlour for twenty minutes; Watson waits
times.quote: Now, Mr. Brown, I am quite at your disposal.

times.label: Thursday evening, twenty minutes later, at dusk: Holmes and Brown reappear; Brown promises to follow instructions
times.quote: It was twenty minutes, and the reds had all faded into greys before Holmes and the trainer reappeared

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes and Watson set off from Mapleton for King's Pyland
times.quote: we set off for King's Pyland

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night (Holmes's reading): the horse, alone, crosses the wet hollow towards Mapleton
times.quote: The track of a horse was plainly outlined in the soft earth
times.note: Holmes supposes that the horse broke away during or after the tragedy (¶114). The hollow 'must have been very wet on Monday night' (¶116). The text does not date the tracks more finely.

times.label: A man's track joins the horse's close to Mapleton; the two turn towards King's Pyland
times.quote: A man's track was visible beside the horse's
times.note: The tracks show the horse alone before this point (¶120–121).

times.label: The man and the horse come back again, ending at the asphalt before the Mapleton gates
times.quote: the same tracks coming back again in the opposite direction

times.label: Friday, five in the morning: a call on Silas Brown (Holmes's question to the groom)
times.quote: if I were to call at five o'clock to-morrow morning
times.note: Holmes puts it as a hypothetical question; the story does not say that he will call.

times.label: Brown carries out Holmes's instructions ("It shall be there") (promised)
times.quote: It shall be there.
times.note: Brown's promise; what he will do, and when, is not told.

times.label: Friday: Brown is to hear from Holmes (promised)
times.quote: you shall hear from me to-morrow
times.note: Holmes also says in ¶141 that he will write to Brown.

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes and Watson trudge back from Mapleton towards King's Pyland, talking of Brown
times.quote: remarked Holmes as we trudged along together

times.label: "That morning" (Holmes's account): Silas Brown, first down, sees a strange horse wandering on the moor and goes out to it
times.quote: he perceived a strange horse wandering over the moor
times.note: Holmes's description to Brown, which Brown accepts. The morning after the horse left the stall; the text does not name the day more exactly.

times.label: That morning (Holmes's account): Brown's first impulse is to lead the horse back to King's Pyland
times.quote: his first impulse had been to lead him back to King's Pyland
times.note: Holmes's account; it fits the double track turning towards King's Pyland (t.man_with_horse).

times.label: That morning (Holmes's account): Brown leads the horse back and hides it at Mapleton
times.quote: how he had led it back and concealed it at Mapleton
times.note: Holmes's account; it fits the return track ending at the Mapleton paving (t.man_horse_back). The story does not order it against the police search of Mapleton (t.mapleton_examined).

times.label: Thursday evening: back at Straker's house; Holmes tells the Colonel and the Inspector, in the parlour, that he returns by the night train
times.quote: Not a word more could I draw from him until we were back at the trainer's house

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes leaves the room to put a question to the maid, then returns
times.quote: I have a question which I should like to put to the maid

times.label: "Of late": three of the sheep in the paddock go lame
times.quote: three of them have gone lame, sir
times.note: The lad's word; not dated more closely than 'of late', before Thursday evening.

times.label: Thursday evening: stepping into the carriage, Holmes asks the stable-lad about the sheep
times.quote: As we stepped into the carriage one of the stable-lads held the door open for us

times.label: Thursday night: Holmes and Watson go back to London by the night train (planned)
times.quote: we both go back to London by the night train

times.label: Colonel Ross begins on the turf (twenty years before)
times.quote: I have been on the turf for twenty years

times.label: Silver Blaze's white forehead and mottled off-foreleg are disguised
times.quote: You have only to wash his face and his leg in spirits of wine
times.note: Not said when or by whom. The horse was 'in the hands of a faker' (¶204). Brown asked Holmes 'Should I change it first or not?' (¶140).

times.label: Colonel Ross scratches his other horse and relies on Holmes's word
times.quote: We scratched our other one, and put all hopes on your word
times.note: After Holmes's assurance that the horse would start (¶161), and before the race.

times.label: The day before the race: fifteen to one against Silver Blaze
times.quote: You could have got fifteen to one yesterday
times.note: The price then shortens until the race morning.

times.label: Silver Blaze is sent over to the race as he is
times.quote: took the liberty of running him just as he was sent over
times.note: Holmes's account; not dated more closely than before the race.

times.label: Four days later: Holmes and Watson in the train bound for Winchester
times.quote: Four days later Holmes and I were again in the train, bound for Winchester
times.note: Four days after Thursday; the race was earlier said to be on Tuesday (¶18).

times.label: Race day: Colonel Ross meets them outside Winchester station
times.quote: Colonel Ross met us by appointment outside the station

times.label: Race day: the drive in Ross's drag to the course; talk of the horse and the betting
times.quote: we drove in his drag to the course beyond the town

times.label: Race day: the drag draws up in the enclosure; the card, the ring's odds, the numbers up
times.quote: As the drag drew up in the enclosure near the grand stand

times.label: Race day: a bay horse in Ross's colours canters out from the weighing enclosure past the drag
times.quote: a powerful bay horse swept out from the weighing enclosure and cantered past us

times.label: Race day: the six horses come up the straight; the Mapleton yellow leads halfway
times.quote: half way up the yellow of the Mapleton stable showed to the front

times.label: Race day: Ross's horse passes the post six lengths ahead
times.quote: passed the post a good six lengths before its rival

times.label: Race day: in the weighing enclosure, Holmes shows Silver Blaze and names the horse as Straker's killer
times.quote: as we made our way into the weighing enclosure

times.label: Race day: the bell rings for the next race
times.quote: But there goes the bell

times.label: Race day evening: in a Pullman car back to London, Holmes explains to Ross and Watson
times.quote: We had the corner of a Pullman car to ourselves that evening as we whirled back to London

times.label: Race day evening: the train reaches Clapham Junction
times.quote: This is Clapham Junction, if I am not mistaken

times.label: Race day evening: arrival at Victoria, in less than ten minutes (expected)
times.quote: we shall be in Victoria in less than ten minutes

times.label: Race day evening: a cigar with the Colonel in Holmes and Watson's rooms (offered)
times.quote: If you care to smoke a cigar in our rooms, Colonel
times.note: Holmes's invitation; the story does not say whether Ross comes.

times.label: Monday evening: curried mutton is served at Straker's house and a dish set aside for the stable-boy
times.quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy
times.note: Holmes: only Straker and his wife could have chosen curried mutton for supper that night.

times.label: Monday evening: the opium is added to the stable-boy's dish (Holmes's reasoning)
times.quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy
times.note: Holmes asks which of Straker and his wife had access to the dish without the maid seeing them; so before she carries it down.

times.label: Monday night: Simpson, in his flight from the stables, drops his cravat (Holmes's account)
times.quote: Simpson in his flight had dropped his cravat

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: Straker picks up the cravat (Holmes's account)
times.quote: Straker had picked it up
times.note: Holmes guesses he meant to use it in securing the horse's leg. The text does not say exactly when or where he found it.

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: Straker leads the horse out to the hollow, where his light would be invisible (Holmes's account)
times.quote: Straker had led out the horse to a hollow where his light would be invisible

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: in the hollow, Straker gets behind the horse and strikes a light (Holmes's account)
times.quote: Once in the hollow, he had got behind the horse and had struck a light

times.label: Straker practises the tendon-nicking on the sheep (Holmes's surmise)
times.quote: would not undertake this delicate tendon-nicking without a little practice
times.note: Holmes's surmise, which the lame sheep bear out; not dated.

times.label: Straker leads a double life as "Derbyshire", with a second establishment and an extravagant wife who runs him into debt
times.quote: an excellent customer of the name of Derbyshire, who had a very dashing wife
times.note: Holmes's conclusion (¶225) and the milliner's word (¶229); not dated, before the Monday night.

times.label: After returning to London: Holmes calls on the milliner with Straker's photograph
times.quote: When I returned to London I called upon the milliner
times.note: Between the night train back and the return from the race; not ordered against the trip to Winchester more finely.

times.label: Edith Baxter makes her sworn statement
times.quote: The girl has sworn

times.label: The answer to Holmes's special wire reaches him
times.quote: to clear the matter up

times.label: The police find traces of the gypsies' camp
times.quote: We have found traces which show that a party of gypsies encamped
times.note: Before the drive of Thursday evening; not otherwise dated.

times.label: A ten-pound note is found in Simpson's purse
times.quote: One was found in his purse.
times.note: Before the drive of Thursday evening.

times.label: Thursday evening: Holmes steps out of the landau at the villa; talk outside before going in
times.quote: he roused himself with a violent start and stepped out of the carriage

times.label: Monday–Tuesday night: after the kick, the horse bolts (Holmes's account)
times.quote: Ah, it bolted
times.note: Holmes's account; before he crosses the wet hollow alone (t.horse_alone_hollow), which the text does not order explicitly.
